discovery: Quantum cryptography: quantum key distribution and the use of entanglement as a resource for secure communication

nominees.name: Charles H. Bennett
nominees.affiliation: IBM Thomas J. Watson Research Center, Yorktown Heights, USA

nominees.name: Artur Ekert
nominees.affiliation: University of Oxford, UK, and Centre for Quantum Technologies, National University of Singapore

motivation: Bennett and Brassard (BB84) showed that the quantum properties of single photons, namely that measurement disturbs them and they cannot be cloned, can make communication secure because of the laws of physics. Ekert (1991) showed independently that entanglement itself can be used to distribute keys, and he linked security directly to the violation of Bell inequalities. This turned the foundational question raised by Einstein, Podolsky, Rosen and Bell into a working resource. Bennett and Brassard also co-invented quantum teleportation (1993), which experimentalists then realised. Their ideas founded quantum information science. Today they underpin fibre networks, the 1200 km satellite-to-ground links of Micius and device-independent cryptography. Few theoretical ideas have changed how experimental quantum physics is done so deeply, or built such a large international community.
